memos.headline: Momentum Leaders GOOGL, UNH, AMZN Stretched to Extremes; XOM and JPM Show Relative Weakness
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape today: GOOGL (RSI 84, +24% above 50d), UNH (RSI 80, +23% above 50d), and AMZN (RSI 75, +18% above 50d) are all at or near 52-week highs with extraordinary relative strength versus SPY, but the degree of extension raises near-term mean-reversion risk. NVDA and CAT sit in a healthier momentum sweet spot—strong trends, RSI in the mid-60s, and solid relative strength without the same parabolic stretch. On the weak side, XOM is breaking down with RSI 37, nearly 16% off its high, and negative relative strength of roughly -14% over both 4- and 12-week windows; MSFT remains 23% below its 52-week high and still trades below its 200-day mean despite a recent 4-week bounce. I favor NVDA and CAT as the cleanest trend-following longs, would wait for a pullback in GOOGL and UNH before adding, and would avoid XOM until it reclaims its 50-day average.

views.note: Strong uptrend near highs with RSI 66, +6.6% 12w relative strength vs SPY, and not yet overextended—would reassess on a close below 190 (roughly the 50d mean).
Massive 26w gain of +54%, RSI 67 still manageable, +9.2% 12w relative strength; risk is the +49% premium to 200d mean, so I'd tighten stops on a break below 830.
RSI 84 and +24% above 50d mean signal extreme overbought conditions despite outstanding relative strength; I'd wait for a pullback toward 370 before initiating.
RSI 80 and +23% above 50d mean after a +36% 12w rally is too stretched for new money; a retest of 350 would be a better entry.
Near highs with dominant 12w relative strength of +27%, but RSI 75 and +18% above 50d suggest waiting for a consolidation toward 250.
At a new 52w high with RSI 73 and +12% above 50d; trend is fine but 12w relative strength vs SPY is flat, so it's a hold rather than a fresh add.
RSI 37, -16% from highs, -7% below 50d, and -14% relative strength vs SPY over 4w and 12w—clear downtrend; would reconsider only above 155.
Still 23% below 52w high and trading 11% under its 200d mean; the 4w bounce is encouraging but trend remains broken until it clears 440.
Negative returns across all timeframes, RSI 45, and -11% 4w relative strength vs SPY; needs to hold 295 or risk further deterioration.
Persistent underperformance with -15% 12w relative strength vs SPY, below both moving averages, and 14% off highs; no reason to own until trend inflects above 152.

memos.headline: GOOGL and MSFT Lead on Margin Expansion; XOM and UNH Flash Earnings-Power Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between names with accelerating, durable earnings power and those facing cash-flow compression. GOOGL stands out most: Q1 revenue grew +21.8% YoY to $109.9B while net income surged +81.2% to $62.6B, pushing net margin to an extraordinary 56.9% on minimal debt of $14.8B—this is the best margin profile in the group by far. MSFT posted +18.3% revenue growth and +23.1% net income growth with a 38.3% net margin and only $40.3B of debt, confirming durable cloud-driven earnings expansion. On the other side, XOM's net income collapsed -45.8% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin, and UNH barely grew revenue (+2.0%) while net income slipped -0.2%, signaling medical-cost headwinds are compressing profitability. I would need to see XOM's upstream realization prices stabilize and UNH's medical-loss ratio improve before reconsidering either name.

views.note: Net margin of 56.9% with +81.2% YoY net income growth and only $14.8B debt is the strongest earnings-power profile in the universe.
Revenue +18.3% and net income +23.1% YoY with 38.3% net margin and moderate $40.3B debt demonstrate durable, high-quality earnings growth.
FY26 revenue +73.2% and 63.1% net margin on just $8.5B debt are extraordinary, though the data is now three months stale and I need the upcoming quarter to confirm sustainability.
Net income surged +76.7% YoY to $30.3B and margin expanded to 16.7%, but $122.6B of total debt keeps me slightly cautious on leverage.
Revenue +22.2% and net income +27.2% YoY with a 14.6% margin show strong cyclical momentum, though I'd watch backlog trends for durability.
Revenue +16.6% and 26.6% margin are solid but $82.7B debt is notable and net income growth of +19.4% lags peers like GOOGL and MSFT.
Steady +10% revenue and +12.6% net income growth with a 33.1% margin are respectable for a bank, but credit-cycle risk keeps me from going overweight.
Revenue +7.4% and 18.5% margin are fine for a staple, but +4.3% net income growth barely keeps pace with inflation—no reason to pay up.
Net income down -45.8% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% margin signals severe earnings compression; I need upstream realizations to recover before reconsidering.
Revenue growth of just +2.0% and flat net income (-0.2% YoY) on $77.9B of debt suggest medical-cost pressures are eroding earnings power.

memos.headline: Fed on Extended Pause at 3.75% as Sticky 3.3% CPI Keeps Easing Off the Table—Favor Banks and Staples Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has sat at 3.75% for three months with no change, even after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year. CPI running at 3.3% YoY—well above target—explains the reluctance to cut further, while the unemployment rate at 4.3% (flat for three months, only +10 bps YoY) signals a labor market that is softening gently but not cracking. The 10y yield at 4.38% has risen 16 bps over three months and the 10y-2y spread has compressed 23 bps to +49 bps, suggesting the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and a flatter curve. This regime favors short-duration earners—banks benefit from a positively sloped curve and stable short rates, while staples hold up in a slowing-but-not-recessionary backdrop; I am cautious on long-duration growth names whose valuations are pressured by rising real yields. A CPI print falling below 3.0% or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would shift my call toward renewed easing and rotate me back into growth.

views.note: Positive curve slope of 49 bps and stable fed funds support net interest income in a pause regime.
Defensive staples outperform in a late-cycle pause with sticky inflation and modest labor softening.
Energy is a mixed bag—inflation supports pricing power but a gently softening economy caps demand upside.
Rising 10y yields (+16 bps in 3m) and higher-for-longer rates compress long-duration growth multiples.
Quality growth with cash flow resilience, but 10y at 4.38% limits multiple expansion; not compelling either way.
Similar duration sensitivity as AAPL; recurring revenue provides a floor but higher-for-longer caps upside.
Consumer-facing cyclicality plus long-duration profile is a poor combination with sticky CPI and rising long yields.
Ad revenue is cyclically exposed but strong cash generation offsets; net effect is roughly neutral in a pause.
Cyclical bellwether faces headwinds from a gently softening labor market, though infrastructure spend provides a floor.
Defensive healthcare with pricing power in an inflationary pause; less rate-sensitive than growth tech.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Price Reactions Flag GOOGL and CAT as Positive Sentiment Standouts; MSFT Tone Deteriorating
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as the best available proxy for sentiment shifts across the universe this cycle. GOOGL (+10.0%) and CAT (+9.9%) posted the strongest one-day moves on their Q-results 8-Ks, signaling a decisive positive narrative shift that likely has further room to run in media tone. UNH (+7.0%) and AAPL (+3.2%) also saw constructive reactions, though UNH's move is now two-plus weeks old and may be largely priced. MSFT stands out negatively with a -3.9% reaction to its earnings 8-K, suggesting the market read the results as a disappointment and media tone is likely to stay pressured near-term. JPM's muted -0.8% on earnings plus a fresh 8-K on May 7 flagging material modifications to security-holder rights adds governance noise that could weigh on sentiment.

views.note: A +10.0% earnings-day pop is the largest in the universe and signals a sharp positive narrative shift that media coverage should amplify.
A +9.9% earnings-day reaction reflects a strong positive sentiment inflection, supported by multiple pre-earnings 8-K disclosures that kept the name in the news flow.
The -3.9% post-earnings drop is the worst reaction in the universe and points to a negative tone trajectory that may not yet be fully reflected.
The +7.0% earnings pop was strong but occurred on April 21, so the positive sentiment impulse is aging and conviction is lower.
A solid +3.2% earnings reaction is constructive but modest relative to GOOGL/CAT, and a director change 8-K adds minor governance noise.
Earnings reaction was a mild -0.8%, and the May 7 8-K on material modifications to security-holder rights introduces governance uncertainty that could keep tone flat.
A -1.0% earnings reaction plus a subsequent director-change 8-K suggest mildly negative sentiment drift with no clear catalyst to reverse it.
The +0.8% earnings reaction is essentially flat, and while high 8-K filing volume kept AMZN in the news, there is no clear directional sentiment signal.

memos.headline: Oil at $98 and Policy Uncertainty Surging Signal Geopolitical Supply-Side Stress; Favor Energy, Caution on Trade-Exposed Tech and Industrials
memos.body: I see a bifurcated geopolitical picture as of today. WTI crude has surged 54% over three months to $98.38/bbl, pointing to a structural energy-supply disruption—likely sanctions-related or Middle East-driven—even as the one-month pullback of 14% suggests some near-term de-escalation or demand concern. The Economic Policy Uncertainty Index jumped 31% month-over-month to 318, yet is still down 39% from its three-month-ago peak, which tells me we are in a second wave of policy shock rather than a fresh crisis. Credit markets remain sanguine with HY OAS at 2.79% (tightening 33bp over the month), and VIX has collapsed 34% to 17, so equity vol is not pricing the tail risk that the uncertainty index implies. My key concern is that any escalation in sanctions, export controls (especially on semiconductors to China), or energy embargoes could re-widen spreads quickly; a reversal in the VIX-to-EPU divergence would be the signal. I would need to see WTI sustainably above $100 or a new round of semiconductor export restrictions to upgrade conviction on the downside for NVDA and AAPL.

views.note: WTI at $98 with a 54% three-month surge directly benefits XOM's upstream margins; sustained geopolitical supply disruption is structural until sanctions ease.
Policy uncertainty at 318 with a rising monthly trend raises the probability of tighter semiconductor export controls to China, which would hit NVDA's data-center revenue disproportionately.

Supply-chain concentration in China remains a structural vulnerability, but VIX at 17 and tight credit spreads suggest the market is not pricing imminent disruption; I lack a catalyst to go directional.

High oil prices support mining/energy capex but elevated policy uncertainty and potential tariff escalation cloud the export outlook; multiple recent 8-Ks suggest management is actively managing disclosure around these risks.

Tight HY spreads and a positive 10y-2y curve at 49bp support bank NII; geopolitical volatility also tends to boost trading revenue, and JPM's frequent 8-K filings suggest proactive capital-markets activity.
Defensive staples benefit from uncertainty, but $98 oil raises input-cost pressure on packaging and transport; Reg FD disclosures in April may reflect margin guidance adjustments.
